name: Daifuku
description: Daifuku opens a grid of AI agent terminals with one key and colours each window's border by what its agent is doing.

hero.lede: Daifuku opens a grid of AI agent terminals with one key and colours each window's border by what its agent is doing.
notes: For Windows 10 and 11 with Windows Terminal, on an account that is an administrator. On an ARM PC, take the ARM64 version. Both also come as a zip: x64, ARM64.
If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Daifuku runs on Windows. Open this page on your PC to download it.

features.label: Next
features.title: One key to the waiting agent
body: <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+N</kbd> brings up the agent that has waited longest, then the failed ones. Press it again for the next one.
Yellow means waiting, red failed, blue working and green done.

main.name: f1
main.alt: The three waiting terminals brought to the front

features.label: Setup
features.title: Double-click to install
body: Double-click daifuku.exe, press Enter and allow it. It copies itself to Program Files, lists itself in Settings, Apps and starts at every sign-in.
daifuku doctor checks the whole setup and says how to fix anything that is off.

main.name: f2
main.alt: daifuku doctor with every check passing

features.label: Scripts
features.title: Every command speaks JSON
body: Add --json and a command prints one JSON document, errors included. A script or an assistant reads each agent's state from daifuku status --json.

main.name: f3
main.alt: daifuku status --json and the same output as a table of agents and states

features.label: Colours
features.title: Readable to every eye
body: Every state has its own border width, so the states read without colour. A colour-blind palette is one line in the config.

main.name: f5
main.alt: The grid with the colour-blind palette

assistant.label: Config
assistant.title: Every key is optional
body: The defaults work without editing. daifuku config opens the file, and the daemon picks up every saved change within two seconds.
Set how many terminals a fleet opens, on which monitor, in which folder and with which key. daifuku config validate checks the file the way the daemon reads it.
assistant.caption: C:\ProgramData\Daifuku\daifuku.json

items: A fleet can fill half its monitor, or any part of it, with the area key.
The with key opens a second fleet together with the first.
daifuku spawn opens a single agent terminal, and daifuku restore brings those back after Windows restarts.
daifuku wait waits until an agent finishes its turn.
The priority key runs a fleet's agents at a lower priority, and nothing they start outlives the terminal.

requirements: An account that is an administrator itself

privacy.title: Nothing goes online
body: Daifuku has no network access, no telemetry and no update check. Agents report their state over a local pipe on your PC.

data.title: One folder for config and logs
body: The config, the saved state and a log a day live in C:\ProgramData\Daifuku. The program itself is in C:\Program Files\Daifuku.

keys: Open the fleet in its grid
Go to the agent waiting longest
Put every terminal back in its cell
keys_note: Global keys, all of them changeable in the config.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Double-click it, press Enter and allow it.
Press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+Enter</kbd> to open your first fleet.

basics.title: Updates
body: Download the new daifuku.exe and double-click it again. Your config and hooks are kept.

basics.title: Removing it
body: Settings, Apps, Installed apps, the three dots next to Daifuku, Uninstall. Config and logs stay; daifuku uninstall --purge from an administrator terminal removes those too.

a: Yes. It is open source under the GPL-3.0 licence.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Daifuku is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about it the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.

faq.q: Can I try it without an agent?
a: Yes. daifuku demo from an administrator terminal opens six scripted agents.

faq.q: Why does it need administrator rights?
a: The daemon runs as administrator so that no ordinary program can change what it starts, and fleets open as administrator by default. "admin": false on a fleet opens its terminals as you.
In C:\ProgramData\Daifuku: the config, the saved state and the logs. Nothing leaves your PC.
